turns.content: I don't understand why jet engines are dangerous even when they're just sitting there at idle. With a prop plane I can see if it's running.

That's exactly the key difference. A jet engine has no visible spinning propeller to warn you it's running. Even at idle, the intake is pulling in enough air to suck a nearby person into the fan, and the exhaust is blowing hot, fast-moving air that can knock a person down. You must treat any jet engine as potentially running and stay clear of both the intake and exhaust areas at all times.

turns.content: For my checkride, what should I know about adding power when taxiing a jet airplane?

You need to demonstrate awareness that adding too much power can lift debris off the ground and cause foreign object damage to the engine or injury to people nearby. Additionally, jet blast from taxiing into parking areas can affect loose ground equipment behind the aircraft. The guidance is to exercise caution when adding power to start moving and to avoid excessive power during taxi.

turns.content: I figure ramp safety around jets is basically the same as around props. You just watch for the spinning blades and stay clear.

That assumption is actually dangerous with jets. Unlike a propeller, a jet engine gives no visual indication that it is running. Even at idle it creates enough intake suction to pull a person into the fan and enough exhaust force to blow a person down. You cannot rely on visual cues the way you can with a propeller, so you must treat every jet engine as potentially running and maintain safe distances from both ends.

turns.content: What exactly does jet blast do when you're taxiing into a parking area? Why does it matter?

When a jet airplane taxis into a parking area, the exhaust blast behind the aircraft is moving fast enough to affect loose ground equipment in that area. This means items like cones, chocks, or other unsecured equipment can be blown around, creating hazards for ground personnel and other aircraft. Pilots should be aware of what is behind them before adding power in confined ramp areas.
